newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI pushes down rupee against forward dollar.
newsitem.headline: India RBI pushes down rupee against forward dollar.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) bought forward dollars of wide maturities on Thursday, lifting the forward premiums, dealers said.
"They didn't buy as much as they did yesterday," said a dealer at a foreign bank. He said RBI bought May, September and October dollars in outright deals on Thursday.
On Wednesday RBI bought over $150 million, dealers said.
The six month annualised forward premium closed the day at 6.92 percent, up from the previous close of 6.63 percent.
"I expect the forward premium (six month) to move up to 7.0 percent and then fall back," R.K. Das, chief of forex and treasury at Adani Exports Ltd told Reuters on Thursday.
He said most Indian exporters were reconciled to an overvalued rupee. Exporters continued to sell their forward dollars on Thursday to take advantage of the rising premiums.
"I am looking to receiving (premium for selling forward dollars) at these levels," Yeshwant Rao, deputy general manager (forex) at textiles firm Arvind Mills said.
Dealers said the RBI purchased spot dollars also towards the end of trading at 35.85 level.
The spot rupee closed at 35.8450/8550 against the dollar.
